changes.decision: Adding a named clip copies its definition into a fresh video-owned occurrence. Preserve underlying source-media references without implying media-file duplication. Persist that independent definition with the video; later library edits never alter it. An origin association serves explicit Update Named Clip only. Retain staged Add, explicit confirmation, atomic failure, insertion placement, collision handling and commit freeze.

Present a copied composed clip as one grouped timeline object. Selection and applicable edits operate on that group until explicit Ungroup; do not expose its internal parts as independently editable beforehand. Preserve composition-wide range scope and existing whole-object track scope. Keep the library vocabulary Video Files, Clips, Videos and Playlists; assembly is neither another content category nor an editor mode.

Extend existing trim semantics to the complete group. Inward trimming retains excluded component references; outward trimming restores retained content and may extend into available source-file content at the corresponding edge. Preserve inclusive boundaries, source bounds, time-zero/preceding-neighbor limits, forward collision-only End push, shortening gaps, synchronized preview and one undoable trim. Saving and reopening must retain this restoration capability.

Keep explicit Update Named Clip for one associated occurrence whose temporal trim differs. Compare saved and proposed Start/End, then confirm a library-definition change preserving its identity. Explain that only future additions use it; all existing occurrences, including the selected copy and locally trimmed copies, stay unchanged. Crop, volume, mute and track settings remain excluded. Remove follower updates and downstream collision checks. Preserve stopped-preview context, commit freeze, success identification, and dialog/target/draft/selection retention on failure or cancellation.

Remove obsolete follower/override inventories and collision messaging from the update dialog. Retire the existing collision question and trace gap, removing their unresolved dependencies while retaining identity/history. Reuse shared-clip-review evidence only for explicit local-versus-library editing and review before confirmation; replace its superseded propagation adaptations. Existing source observations remain evidence about those products, not authority for linked behavior here.

Add one contextual Ungroup command for a selected grouped clip through the existing selection menu and keyboard access. Materialize included parts as separate timeline clips; omit wholly excluded parts and preserve the current effective trim at partial boundaries. Selected working UX is one draft operation with synchronized selection/preview and Undo/Redo; failure preserves the prior group. Do not invent track placement or transfer of group framing/audio while those semantics remain unresolved.

On canonical follow-through, retain existing record identities and bind the affected realizations to supplied product revision 7. Add trace coverage for grouped editing. Reuse unchanged shell, four-track composition, guards, playback, export, visual constraints and independent inspection behavior.

questions: Ungroup placement: a saved composed clip may contain simultaneous parts from several tracks. Which destination tracks and timing preserve those parts while satisfying four-track capacity and no same-track overlap? What happens when destination tracks are occupied?

Ungroup appearance and sound: how do group source crop, volume/mute and destination-track framing/audio transfer to materialized parts without an unintended output change? Product and architecture must resolve the representation and feasibility.

Grouped trim: where several parts meet an outer edge, which source ranges extend, and how are exhaustion and gaps presented? Existing research does not establish this combined group/ungroup behavior; obtain bounded pattern research before promoting the detailed interaction.

Retain existing unresolved source-ownership, media-repair, cross-source-playback, export-app-close and video-expansion-settings-conflict questions. The propagation-collision question is retired, not carried forward.
